subject.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs

question: Should existing file-transfer policy entries beginning with `~\` become active home-relative authorization rules?
rationale: The code is mechanically sound and well-proven, but automation cannot decide whether previously non-matching stored authorization strings should gain this supported meaning.

options.title: Accept Windows tilde syntax
options.body: Treat `~\` as equivalent to `~/` and explicitly accept the stored-policy reinterpretation.

options.title: Require portable slash syntax
options.body: Keep `~\` literal and document `~/` as the only supported home-relative policy form.

recommendation.title: Accept Windows tilde syntax
recommendation.body: Treat `~\` as equivalent to `~/` and explicitly accept the stored-policy reinterpretation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available decision owner from the canonical file-transfer authorization review and merge history.
